headline: Blood cells from 80-year-old donor become stem cells with molecular age under 20
summary: Scientists have achieved a remarkable feat, reprogramming blood cells from an 80-year-old into stem cells with a molecular age equivalent to someone under 20. This breakthrough could revolutionize regenerative medicine.
details: Scientists have achieved a significant milestone, successfully reprogramming blood cells from an 80-year-old donor. These cells were transformed into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) that exhibit a molecular age equivalent to less than 20 years old. This dramatic age reversal highlights the plasticity of human cells.

The research involved specific genetic reprogramming techniques, essentially resetting the epigenetic clock within the cells. This process effectively erased decades of cellular aging markers, demonstrating a profound rejuvenation at a molecular level. The methodology builds on previous work in cellular reprogramming.

This breakthrough has immense implications for regenerative medicine, offering new possibilities for treating age-related diseases and injuries. By creating youthful, patient-specific stem cells, researchers could develop therapies for conditions like heart disease, neurodegenerative disorders, and organ failure without immune rejection.

Further studies are needed to understand the long-term stability and functionality of these rejuvenated cells in vivo. The next steps involve exploring the safety and efficacy of using such reprogrammed cells for therapeutic applications. This research paves the way for future anti-aging interventions.

headline_marked: [[Janas-LLM runs 80B models]] on 32GB RAM laptops, 13x faster than llama.cpp
headline: Janas-LLM runs 80B models on 32GB RAM laptops, 13x faster than llama.cpp
summary: Janas-LLM achieves 37 tokens/s for a 48GB Qwen3-Next-80B model on a 32GB laptop, significantly outperforming llama.cpp's 2.8 tokens/s on the same hardware.
details: Janas-LLM, a new C-based tool, enables running large mixture-of-experts language models (LLMs) like the 48GB Qwen3-Next-80B on ordinary laptops with just 32GB of RAM. It achieves impressive speeds, hitting 37 tokens/s for generation and 62 tokens/s for prompt reading on benchmarked hardware.

This performance significantly surpasses existing solutions like llama.cpp, which managed only 2.8 tokens/s for generation and 16 tokens/s for prompt reading with the same Qwen3-Next-80B model on the identical laptop setup. Janas-LLM was faster than llama.cpp on nearly every model tested.

The tool's innovation lies in its ability to stream model weights directly from an NVMe SSD, keeping only the currently needed "experts" in memory. Frequently accessed experts are cached, allowing models much larger than available RAM to run efficiently.

Benchmarks were conducted on a Debian 13 Linux laptop featuring an Intel Core Ultra 9 185H processor, its integrated Arc GPU, 32 GB of RAM, and an NVMe SSD. Janas-LLM also supports Windows 10/11 x86-64, showing comparable performance.
Janas-LLM is part of a family of AI tools written in C with minimal dependencies. It comes with pre-converted models from Hugging Face, simplifying setup for users.

Users have control over memory usage with the --cache option and can disable GPU acceleration entirely using JANAS_GPU=0. The engine dynamically optimizes its choices for each machine, adapting to different hardware configurations.

While extensively tested on Intel Core Ultra systems, the developers encourage users to run janas-bench on other CPUs (AMD, without AVX-VNNI), discrete GPUs, or different memory/disk setups to gather more performance data and help improve the tool's adaptability.
